transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I feel like I’ve been stuck in this low, heavy mood for years and I just don’t enjoy anything the way I used to. It's gotten to the point where my husband and coworkers have really started to notice and worry about me.
How long have you been feeling this way? Specifically, have you had times when your mood improved for more than a few weeks before going back down?

This low, heavy feeling has been with me steadily for a little over two years now, ever since my workload increased and I started caring for my mom. I haven't really had any breaks from it at all. It's just been constant, without any times where my mood improved for more than a week or two.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt clearly better and more like your usual self, even if things were still stressful?

No, I definitely haven't had a break like that. This low, heavy feeling has been completely constant over the last two-plus years without any real relief. I haven't felt like my usual self for even a few weeks, let alone two whole months.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F34.1", "F33"], but based on this conversation, F33 (recurrent depressive disorder) seems unlikely because the patient reports a persistent, continuous low mood for over two years without any clear remission lasting at least two months. This course is more consistent with a chronic mood disturbance, which supports F34.1 (dysthymia). There is no history of a symptom-free interval, which is required for F33. Therefore, the current candidate is now only F34.1.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic, low-grade depressed mood lasting for over two years without any symptom-free intervals longer than a few weeks, meeting the duration and symptom criteria for persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). The absence of a two-month period of remission rules out major depressive disorder in remission, and there is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes.
